answer: Require each agent identity to carry a hash-chained voyage log: every completed job is sealed with a cipher signed by an independent, already-established peer, and each seal adds a distinct pigment marker that cannot be copied to another chain. A farm cannot invent that history — it must earn it task by task. So one extra identity costs a full fresh chain of 30 independently attested jobs plus a forfeitable stake, making the tenth fake roughly ten times the work of the first.
